record.paper_title: Negative (and Positive) Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.context_brief: edge cover for positive directed cycles
record.original_question: For a signed digraph, determine the smallest number of edges that meet every positive directed cycle.

evidence.quote: Qn. 1+ What is the smallest number of edges that cover all positive cycles? (Reminder: Not necessarily all positive circles!)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed digraph is a pair (D, σ) where D = (V, E) is a directed graph (loops and parallel edges allowed) and σ : E → {+1, −1} is an assignment of a sign to each arc. A directed cycle in D is a sequence of arcs forming a closed directed walk in which no vertex is repeated; the sign of a directed cycle C is the product ∏_{e ∈ C} σ(e), and C is called positive if its sign equals +1.

Given a signed digraph (D, σ), an edge set F ⊆ E is said to cover all positive directed cycles if every positive directed cycle of D contains at least one arc of F. Define
  τ⁺(D, σ) := min { |F| : F ⊆ E covers every positive directed cycle of (D, σ) }.

Determine τ⁺(D, σ): give a formula, exact characterization, sharp bounds, or an effective algorithm for computing the minimum number of arcs needed to meet every positive directed cycle of an arbitrary finite signed digraph (D, σ). (Note: only positive directed cycles need to be covered, not arbitrary positive closed walks or undirected positive circles.)
artifact.status_search_result: Related decision and optimization problems on covering cycles in signed digraphs (e.g., positive/negative feedback vertex and arc set problems) are known to be NP-complete via reductions to even/odd cycle covering in unsigned digraphs. We did not find a dedicated result giving an exact formula or characterization for the minimum number of arcs covering all positive directed cycles, so the problem appears to remain open as a structural/extremal question.

status_evidence.title: On the complexity of feedback set problems in signed digraphs
status_evidence.snippet: The positive feedback vertex/arc set problems in signed digraphs are shown to be NP-complete via reductions to even/odd cycle covering.
status_evidence.claim: Covering all positive (or negative) cycles in a signed digraph by a minimum vertex/arc set is NP-complete, suggesting no easy closed-form answer.

status_evidence.title: Signed graph - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The sign of a cycle is the product of the signs of its edges; balance and covering questions are central in signed graph theory.
status_evidence.claim: Standard definitions of positive cycles in signed graphs/digraphs match the formulation of the problem.
